summary.overview: The team agreed to move the mobile app's public launch to March 3 to make room for offline mode, and to defer in-app chat to v1.1. The launch marketing budget is still open: the deck shows $120,000, but finance says $95,000 was approved.
key_points: Offline mode stays in v1, and it is the main reason the launch date moved.
The internal beta stays on January 10.
In-app chat moves to v1.1 because the message service isn't built yet.
Launch events spend is on hold until finance confirms the budget.
App store review in February may take longer than the plan allows.

decisions.text: Move the public launch from February 14 to March 3.
Keep the internal beta on January 10.
Defer in-app chat to v1.1 and say so in the launch notes.
Hold launch events spend until finance confirms the budget.

Even one-to-one chat needs a message service and moderation backend that don't exist yet. Too risky next to offline mode.

conflicts.description: The risks slide allows 5 days for app store review. Marcus suggested submitting at least 10 days before launch. The plan wasn't updated.

transcript.text: Thanks everyone. Today we need to lock the launch plan for the mobile app, agree the marketing budget, and settle what goes into v1.
As you can see on the slide, the target is a public launch on February 14th, with the internal beta on January 10th.
I have to be honest, February 14th isn't realistic if offline mode stays in scope. Sync conflict handling alone is three to four weeks. Realistically we're looking at early March.
How early? I need a date I can give marketing.
March 3rd. That includes two weeks of hardening after the beta.
A slip to March is fine from finance's side, as long as the campaign spend moves with it.
Okay. Let's move the public launch to March 3rd and keep the internal beta on January 10th. I'll update the deck.
Next, budget. The slide shows a hundred and twenty thousand for launch marketing: seventy for paid ads, thirty for influencers, twenty for events.
That number is out of date. What finance approved last week was ninety-five thousand, not one-twenty. The events line was cut.
That's news to me. The one-twenty came from the October planning review.
October was before the reforecast. I'd plan around ninety-five until we hear otherwise.
If events are cut, we need to know soon. The booth design work is already scheduled.
Let's not decide this in the room. Tom, can you confirm the final number with finance by Monday? We'll hold the events spend until then.
Scope for v1. The slide lists offline mode, dark mode and in-app chat.
I'd really push to keep chat in v1. It's the top request in the beta survey, and the support team is counting on it to cut email volume.
I get that, but chat needs a moderation backend and push infrastructure we haven't built. Shipping it in the same release as offline mode is too much risk.
Could we ship a reduced version? One-to-one support chat only, no group threads.
Even one-to-one needs the message service. That's the expensive part, not the threads.
I'm hearing chat can't be done safely by March 3rd. Let's defer in-app chat to v1.1 and say so clearly in the launch notes. Elena, is that workable?
Workable. Not my preference, but I agree the date matters more.
Dark mode, on the other hand, is cheap. I can have the full specs ready by early December.
On risks: app store review times in February are unpredictable, so we should submit at least ten days before launch.
And I'll have a proper estimate for offline sync by the 28th, so we know whether March 3rd holds.
Great. To recap: launch moves to March 3rd, chat moves to v1.1, and the budget waits on Tom's confirmation. Thanks, all.
